title: P2P-native topology surfaces with EPR/REA contract trace

vision_quotes.text: The substrate is invisible. A visitor cannot tell 'this network actually works.' A steward cannot see 'my devices, my replication, my reciprocity.' An operator cannot see their doorway's projection coverage. Without these views, the protocol's core resilience claim — P2P hosting that doesn't go down — is unverifiable from the surface.
Help communities build spaces that have the intimacy of a group chat and the openness of a public square. And help those spaces connect to each other when it matters.

plan_deliverables.text: Per-content distribution badge — replicas + projectors + reach + health, visible to visitors with no auth
/shefa/cluster — steward's stewarded compute footprint, federated across their device bindings
/shefa/reciprocity — committed-vs-delivered ledger over REA Commitments + EconomicEvents
Storage content distribution 3-tab operator rollup (By Type / By Reach / By Node)
Doorway dashboard topology — federation peers, cache metrics, route registry, local view of connected stewards
EPR/REA contract backing the compute — operator-doorway Commitment substrate visible/traceable through the topology surfaces

manifesto_anchors.why: If the substrate works but cannot be SEEN working, the protocol's resilience claim is unverifiable. Every surface above is the human-visible falsifier for a substrate primitive (custody, stewardship, operator commitment, blob hosting reciprocity).

EPR/REA contract backing compute is the substrate Layer that makes operator authority a notarized social fact, not a server config. The visible surfaces must reflect this — otherwise the architecture is invisible work.
